proposed.choice: Use one embedded SQLite database through node:sqlite in the Node 24 CLI for the first v4 backend.
proposed.rationale: Current handoff records need coherent updates and scoped queries. SQLite replaces the proposed intermediate filesystem adapter while Git remains authoritative for engineering definitions.
alternatives: Implement a filesystem v4 adapter before migrating to SQLite.
Store entire Change documents as opaque database blobs.
Introduce a hosted database for a local checkout.
Add an npm native SQLite addon or move record persistence into a Rust executable, adding a separate binding or packaging boundary for the current local CLI.
consequences: MOD-011 owns relational current records, revisions and project association in .rigorloop/rigorloop.db; selected named attachments remain outside the database.

Select node:sqlite with initial minimum Node 24.15.0 and SQLite 3.51.3, behind the MOD-011 adapter. Its release-candidate API status and bundled-library version require platform qualification; reject older WAL-reset-affected or unqualified builds. Use local WAL/FULL, foreign keys, packaged migrations and supported backup snapshots.

SQLite determines transaction outcomes; callers inspect current context after interruption rather than choosing file-journal complete/restore actions. Existing v3 runtime and its recovery remain version-scoped.
revisit_when: The supported deployment or measured workload exceeds the local SQLite profile.
